cover.text: Gov. Newsom signs an order to plan an AI kill switch for California.

slides.headline: The order Newsom signed Friday
slides.body: On September 18, Gov. Gavin Newsom signed an executive order asking a state panel to recommend AI safety rules within two months — including a kill switch, an emergency shutoff for frontier AI models.

slides.headline: The panel's deadline
slides.numberNote: for the expert panel to deliver its recommendations

slides.headline: What the panel must consider
slides.body: The panel is asked to weigh embedding independent auditors inside AI labs, requiring outside verification of company safety reports, and advancing the kill switch itself, verified by an independent verification organization.

slides.headline: Newsom's case for acting now
slides.quote: We're not waiting to act — we're going to speed up our work on substantial and responsible AI oversight before it's too late.

slides.headline: A kill switch is not a button
slides.body: It would not be a literal switch someone could press. Each major AI lab would instead create and run its own set of protocols to shut down a model, verified on an ongoing basis by an outside organization.
slides.highlight: set of protocols to shut down a model

slides.headline: California's reach has limits
slides.quote: California has only a limited capacity to control what a company incorporated in Delaware does with a data center in Oregon to serve a customer in Colorado.
slides.quoteBy: Max Harms, Machine Intelligence Research Institute

slides.headline: California still shapes what Washington does
slides.body: The SF Standard reports California "sets trends that often end up determining how things get done at the federal level."
slides.highlight: often end up determining how things get done at the federal level

follow: Follow Helios for more on AI regulation and what California is doing about it.
